- Mobile check deposit daily limit: $3,500

### Linked savings boosts
- Link a Green Account (savings): +0.55% APY boost
- Link a Diamond Elite Savings Account: +0.15% APY boost

### How tree planting works (at a glance)
- For every $750 in eligible spending, we plant one tree on your behalf.
- Example: Spend $750 → 1 tree planted; spend 5× that amount → 5 trees planted.

### Foreign ATM withdrawals
- Foreign ATM withdrawal fee: 2% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum of $3.00 per transaction.
- Third-party ATM operator fees may also apply.

### Refer and grow the green community
- Refer others to join Evergreen and earn $35 per successful referral
- New members receive $25 as a welcome bonus
- Earn up to 6 referral bonuses per calendar year

## Quick reference
| Feature | Amount |
|---|---|

| Carbon offset rate | $1.25 g per $1 |
| Checking APY | 0.05% |

| Early direct deposit | Up to 2 days early |
| Mobile deposit daily limit | $3,500 |
| Foreign ATM withdrawal fee | 2% (min $3.00) |
| Green Savings APY boost | +0.55% |
| Diamond Elite Savings APY boost | +0.15% |
| Referral bonus (you earn) | $35 |
| Referral bonus (they receive) | $25 |
| Max referrals per year | 6 |# Evergreen Account specifications and requirements

## Fees and waivers
- Monthly maintenance fee: $6.00
- The monthly maintenance fee is waived when your minimum daily balance is at least $500

## Earnings on balances
- Annual Percentage Yield on your Evergreen Account balance: 0.05%

## Statements
- Paper statements incur a monthly fee of $7.50

## Transaction-related fees
- Returned deposit fee: $17.00
- Incoming domestic wire transfer fee: $12.50

## Purchase and withdrawal limits
- Debit card daily purchase limit: $4,500
- Daily ATM withdrawal limit: $750

## Keeping your account in good standing
- Maintain a minimum daily balance of $500 to avoid the monthly maintenance fee of $6.00
- Choose e‑statements to avoid the paper statement fee of $7.50
- Review deposited items promptly to minimize the chance of a returned deposit fee of $17.00# How the tree-planting program works

## What counts toward planting
- Qualifying posted purchases on your Evergreen Account contribute toward the planting threshold
- Non‑purchase transactions are not counted toward the threshold

## Threshold mechanics
- Your eligible spend is tracked cumulatively
- Each time your running total reaches another multiple of $750, a tree is scheduled for planting
- Any remaining eligible spend below $750 carries forward to your next tree

## Timing and confirmations
- Trees are queued after eligible transactions settle
- You will see confirmations in your environmental impact view once a tree is scheduled

## Tracking progress
- Your tracker shows eligible spend since your last tree and the amount remaining to reach $750# Tracking your environmental impact

## How often your impact is reported
- You receive an environmental impact report on a monthly basis.
- Each report summarizes impact for transactions that posted during that reporting period.

## What your report includes
Your environmental impact report focuses on three key measures:
- Total posted Evergreen Account spend in the period
- Estimated CO2 offset, calculated using $1.25 grams per dollar
- Estimated number of trees planted based on your spend (Rho plants a tree for every $1,000 spent)

## Calculating your CO2 offset
Use this formula to verify or estimate your offset at any time:
- CO2 offset (grams) = Total posted Evergreen spend (USD) × $1.25

Examples:
- $750 spend → 750 × $1.25 grams
- $1,000 spend → 1,000 × $1.25 grams
- $2,500 spend → 2,500 × $1.25 grams

Tip: Convert to larger units if needed
- Kilograms: grams ÷ 1,000
- Metric tons: grams ÷ 1,000,000

## Tracking trees planted
Rho plants one tree for every $1,000 spent.
- To estimate trees: Divide your posted Evergreen spend by 1,000 and take the whole-number result.
  - $750 spend → 0 trees
  - $1,000 spend → 1 tree
  - $2,500 spend → 2 trees
- Your report lists the estimated tree count for the period based on posted transactions.

## Reconciling your report step-by-step
1. Confirm the period: Identify the exact monthly window shown on the report.
2. Sum posted spend: Add all Evergreen Account transactions that posted within the period.
3. Compute offset: Multiply the sum by $1.25 to get total grams of CO2 offset.
4. Count trees: Divide the same spend total by 1,000 and take the whole-number result.
5. Compare: The calculated figures should match your report, subject to the timing considerations below.

## Timing and data considerations
- Pending vs. posted: Only posted transactions are included; pending authorizations are excluded until they post.
- Posting dates: Transactions post on the date they settle, which may differ from the purchase date near period boundaries.
- Refunds/chargebacks: These appear as negative adjustments and reduce both spend and calculated impact within the period in which they post.
- Reversals or corrections: Any corrections posted after the period will be reflected in the subsequent monthly report.

## Keeping your own running totals
- Maintain a simple spreadsheet with two columns: posted spend date and amount.
- At any point, sum the amounts for your target date range and apply:
  - Offset (grams) = Sum × $1.25
  - Trees = floor(Sum ÷ 1,000)
- Save each monthly report alongside your reconciliation for audit and sustainability reporting needs.

# Dark Green Account at a glance

## Snapshot

Quick reference to core details you will use most often.

### Eligibility
- Minimum primary holder age: 17
- Maximum primary holder age: 26

### Fees and rates
- Monthly maintenance fee: $10.00
- Overdraft protection transfer fee: 0
- Out-of-network ATM withdrawal fee: 1% (min $1.50)
- Annual percentage yield (APY): 1.5%

### Rewards and perks
- Student loan payment cashback: 1.25%
- Annual academic standing bonus: $62.50
- Partner textbook retailer discount: 10.0%
- Graduation transition bonus: $100.00

### Limits
- Mobile check deposit daily limit: $1,500

### Direct deposit
- Early direct deposit: 1 day(s) before payday

### Quick tables

#### Eligibility and costs
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum age | 17 |
| Maximum age | 26 |
| Monthly maintenance fee | $10.00 |
| Overdraft protection transfer fee | 0 |
| Out-of-network ATM withdrawal fee | 1% (min $1.50) |

#### Rewards and limits
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| APY | 1.5% |
| Student loan payment cashback | 1.25% |
| Annual academic standing bonus | $62.50 |
| Partner textbook discount | 10.0% |
| Graduation transition bonus | $100.00 |
| Mobile deposit daily limit | $1,500 |
| Early direct deposit | 1 day(s) before payday |

### Notes
- Rewards and limits apply when eligibility conditions are met and verification is provided where required.
- Fees and rates may change with required notice.
- Get paid 1 day(s) early with direct deposit.# Verifying your student enrollment

## How often you must verify
- You must verify your active enrollment per_semester.

## What to prepare
Provide one of the following, ensuring it clearly shows your name, institution, term, and enrollment status:
- An official enrollment letter
- A current class schedule or registration summary
- A student portal screenshot that includes your full name and term details
- A tuition invoice or receipt that lists your status for the term

## How to submit
1. Gather your documentation in a readable format (PDF, image, or clear screenshot).
2. Ensure the document is unredacted and not password-protected.
3. Submit your proof through the secure upload option in your account.

## After you submit
- You will receive a confirmation that your documents were received.
- If additional information is needed, you will be prompted to resubmit with the specific items requested.

## Tips for a successful verification
- Use documents that display your legal name exactly as it appears on your account.
- Include the current term and status; avoid future-dated or undated documents.
- Ensure all essential details are visible and not cropped or blurred.# Earning rewards for good grades

## What you can earn

- Annual cash bonus: You receive $62.50 each year you verify a 3.0+ GPA.
- Savings APY boosts when you qualify:
  - Linked Bronze Savings Account: 0.85% APY boost
  - Linked Platinum Plus Savings Account: 0.45% APY boost
- The boost is added to the standard APY of the eligible linked savings account(s) and applies only while your good‑standing status is active.

## Eligibility criteria

You qualify for rewards when:
- Your most recently completed academic year (or cumulative) GPA is 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale.
- You are the Dark Green Account holder whose name appears on the transcript/verification.
- Your documentation clearly shows your full name, institution, term(s) covered, and GPA.

Notes:
- If your school does not use a 4.0 scale, provide the school’s official scale or conversion so we can confirm the 3.0+ equivalent.
- Part‑time, transfer, and graduate students are eligible as long as GPA can be verified.

## How to verify your GPA

1. Obtain proof of your GPA from your registrar or student portal.
2. Submit your documentation through the Rho-Bank app or secure message center.
3. Ensure your submission includes:
   - Full name matching your account
   - Institution name
   - Term(s) or academic year covered
   - Cumulative or academic‑year GPA
   - Grading scale if not on a 4.0 scale

Accepted documents:
- Official or unofficial transcript (PDF or clear image)
- Registrar letter on school letterhead stating GPA and term(s)
- Third‑party enrollment/GPA verification service results that include your GPA and school source

Tips:
- Combine multiple pages into a single file if needed.
- If you transferred schools, include transcripts from each institution covering the relevant period.

## When rewards are applied

- Review and approval: We typically confirm eligibility shortly after you submit complete documentation.
- Cash bonus: $62.50 is deposited once per 12‑month verification period after approval.
- APY boosts: If you have a linked savings account, the boost begins shortly after approval and remains active for up to 12 months or until your eligibility period ends, whichever comes first.

## Maintaining and renewing your rewards

- Annual re‑verification is required. Submit updated GPA proof each year to continue receiving $62.50 and any applicable APY boosts.
- If your GPA falls below 3.0 for a period, you will not receive the bonus for that verification cycle, and APY boosts will end when the previously verified period expires. You can re‑qualify by submitting new proof once your GPA meets the threshold again.
- If you change or unlink a savings account, any active APY boost applies only to eligible linked accounts going forward.

## Common scenarios

- Pass/Fail or alternative grading: Include the school’s explanation of how performance maps to a 4.0 scale (or an official conversion).
- Quarter vs. semester systems: Provide the transcript summarizing the full academic year or cumulative GPA.
- Transfers: If your GPA resets at the new school, submit the most recent cumulative GPA available; include prior school records if needed to confirm a full academic year at or above 3.0.
- Study abroad: Provide the host or home institution’s transcript showing GPA or the official conversion.
- Graduation mid‑year: Submit your final transcript; you remain eligible for the final verification period if the GPA requirement is met.

## If your submission is declined

Common reasons:
- Missing GPA or grading scale
- Name on the document does not match your account
- Unreadable or incomplete files
- GPA reported is below 3.0

How to fix it:
- Re‑submit a clear, complete document with the required details
- Add the school’s official grading scale or conversion if not on a 4.0 system
- Ensure the name and institution match exactly

Once corrected and approved, your $62.50 and any applicable 0.85% or 0.45% APY boost will be applied for the current verification period.# Student loan payment benefits

## What you earn
- Earn cashback of 1.25% on student loan payments made from your account when they meet eligibility criteria.

## What counts as a qualifying payment
- Direct payments to recognized student loan servicers made from your account
- Payments initiated using standard methods supported by your servicer (for example, electronic payments or mailed checks drawn on your account)

## What does not typically qualify
- Transfers to personal accounts or to individuals that are not loan servicers
- Reimbursements to friends or family for a loan payment they made on your behalf

## EveryonePay considerations
- Payments you send using EveryonePay are subject to a daily limit of $1,000. These person-to-person payments are not treated as direct loan payments to a servicer and typically do not qualify for cashback.

## Posting of rewards
- Cashback is credited after the qualifying payment clears and is identified as a student loan payment to an eligible servicer.# Partner discounts for students

## How the discount works
- When you use your debit card at participating textbook partners, you receive a discount of 10.0% at checkout.

## Getting the discount
1. Confirm the merchant is a participating partner before purchase.
2. Pay with your debit card (physical or digital). Split tender payments may affect discount eligibility.
3. Keep your receipt in case you need to inquire about discount application.

## If a merchant requests a cashier's check
- Some campus-related transactions may require certified funds. If you need a cashier's check, the fee is 5.

## Returns and exchanges
- If you return items, the discount may be reversed or adjusted in line with the merchant's return policy.
- Exchanges processed by the merchant should carry forward the applicable discount when eligible.# Graduating from your Dark Green Account

## Transition overview
- When you move to a regular checking account after you graduate, you can receive a one-time bonus of $100.00.

## When your account transitions
- You can request a transition upon graduation by providing documentation of degree completion or final status.
- If you reach 26, your account will be transitioned to a regular checking account.

## How to claim the bonus
1. Notify us of your graduation and provide acceptable proof (for example, a diploma or official confirmation from your institution).
2. Complete the account transition steps as instructed.
3. Once verified and transitioned, the $100.00 is credited to your account.

## After you transition
- You will receive confirmation of the new account and the posted bonus.
- Features and fees of your new account will apply after the transition is complete.# Why was my Dark Green Account enrollment verification rejected?

## Common reasons for rejection
- The document did not clearly show your name and institution
- The term or status was missing, undated, or listed as in progress
- The image was blurred, cropped, or unreadable
- The file was password-protected or otherwise inaccessible
- The document type was not accepted (for example, a screenshot lacking key details)

## How to fix and resubmit
1. Obtain an official or system-generated document that includes your full name, institution, term, and enrollment status.
2. Capture a clear, full-frame image or export a readable PDF.
3. Ensure the file is not password-protected and that all details are visible.
4. Resubmit your verification using the same upload flow.

## Timing reminder
- You must verify your enrollment per_semester. If your previous term has ended or the documentation is outdated, submit current proof for the active term.# FAQ: Dark Green Account

## Common questions

### Is there a fee if a check I deposited is returned unpaid?
Yes. A returned deposit fee of $10.00 applies when a deposited check is returned unpaid by the issuing bank.

### Do you charge to receive domestic wire transfers?
Yes. Incoming domestic wires are assessed a fee of $7.50.# Dark Green Account Referral Program

## Share the Dark Green experience

Refer others to the Dark Green Account and earn rewards when they join.

### Referral rewards
- **Your bonus**: $40 for each qualifying referral
- **Their bonus**: $30 welcome bonus
- **Maximum per year**: 6 referral bonuses

### Qualification criteria
To qualify for the referral bonus:
1. You must satisfy the 45-day minimum as a Rho-Bank checking customer.
2. The person you refer must open a Dark Green Account
3. They must deposit at least $1,000 within 60 days of opening

### Program details
| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| Referrer bonus | $40 |
| Referred bonus | $30 |
| Annual cap | 6 referrals |
| Minimum deposit | $1,000 |
| Deposit window | 60 days |
| Tenure required | 45 days |

### Bonus payment
- Bonuses are credited within 5-7 business days after qualification
- Both you and the new member must maintain your accounts in good standing

# How Rho calculates carbon offsets

## Calculation model
- For each eligible purchase, Rho multiplies the posted dollar amount by $1.25 to determine grams of CO₂ offset
- Purchase refunds reduce accrued offsets using the same rate of $1.25

## Transaction eligibility rules
- Only eligible purchase transactions accrue offsets
- EveryonePay transfers do not accrue offsets; this applies regardless of the $3,000

## Aggregation and rounding
- Offsets are aggregated over the statement period and rounded to whole grams in your environmental reporting

## Transparency
- The calculation rate used is $1.25 and is displayed within your impact details# Eligibility and fees

## Fee eligibility
- The monthly maintenance fee of $6.00 is waived when your minimum daily balance is at least $500

## Standard fees
- Paper statement fee: $7.50
- Returned deposit fee: $17.00
- Incoming domestic wire transfer fee: $12.50
- Stop payment fee: 25

## How to avoid fees
- Enroll in e‑statements to avoid $7.50
- Maintain the required minimum daily balance of $500 to waive $6.00

## Requests that incur fees
- Placing a stop payment on a check will incur 25# FAQ: Evergreen Account

## Frequently asked questions

### When will I receive my environmental impact report?
You receive impact reports monthly. Reports summarize offsets and related activity for the corresponding period.

### Do all purchases contribute to tree planting and carbon offsets?
Eligible posted purchase transactions count toward both offset calculations and the tree‑planting threshold. Non‑purchase transactions are not included.

### Can I change how often my impact reports are delivered?
Yes. You can adjust your report cadence to align with monthly.

### How do refunds affect my environmental metrics?
Refunds reduce your eligible spend and adjust offset totals accordingly. The change is reflected in your next impact update.

### Where can I see my progress toward the next planted tree?
Your impact view shows eligible spend accumulated since the last tree and how much remains before the next tree is scheduled.

### How does the referral program work?
Refer friends to open an Evergreen Account. The person you refer must deposit at least $750 within 60 days of opening their account to qualify.

### When can I start referring others?
The 45-day tenure threshold applies—calculated from the date you opened your first Rho-Bank checking account.

### How long does the referred person have to make their qualifying deposit?
The referred person must deposit $750 within 60 days of account opening to trigger the referral bonus.# Out-of-network ATM fees for Evergreen Account

## When the fee applies
- You are charged an out-of-network ATM fee when you withdraw cash from an ATM that is not in Rho’s network.
- The fee is assessed per withdrawal transaction.

## Fee structure
- Percentage: 1% of the withdrawal amount
- Maximum per withdrawal: $2.50
- The percentage is applied to the cash dispensed amount. If the percentage-based fee exceeds $2.50, the fee is capped at $2.50.

## Calculation examples
| Cash withdrawal | Percentage fee at 1% | Applied cap | Total out-of-network fee |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $40 | $0.40 | Not reached | $0.40 |
| $250 | $2.50 | Equals cap | $2.50 |
| $600 | $6.00 | Capped at $2.50 | $2.50 |

## How the fee is charged and displayed
- The fee is deducted from your account in addition to the cash withdrawn.
- You will see a separate line item for the out-of-network ATM fee on your transaction history, reflecting the amount calculated using 1% and the $2.50 cap.

## Important notes
- The ATM operator may charge its own surcharge. That surcharge is separate from Rho’s out-of-network fee and is not subject to the $2.50 cap.
- Multiple withdrawals in the same day each incur a separate fee, calculated individually using 1% and capped at $2.50 per withdrawal.

## Tips to reduce or avoid the fee
- Use in-network ATMs to avoid out-of-network charges.
- If you need a larger amount of cash, consider a single withdrawal rather than multiple smaller withdrawals to avoid multiple per-withdrawal fees.

# Wire transfers for Bluest members

## Domestic wires
- You receive 10 complimentary domestic wire transfers each month.
- Incoming domestic wires are credited with a fee of $0.00.

## International wires
- Outbound international wire transfers are assessed a fee of $12.50 per transfer.

## EveryonePay daily limit
- The EveryonePay daily send limit is $7,500.

### Practical tips
- Track your monthly domestic wire usage so you can take full advantage of the 10 complimentary transfers.
- Use EveryonePay for eligible person-to-person transfers that fit within the $7,500 daily limit.
- For international transfers, plan around the $12.50 per transfer cost.# What happens if my balance falls below the minimum?

## Impact of falling below the required balance
- If your daily balance drops below $112,500, a monthly maintenance fee of $75.00 will be assessed.

## How to restore benefits
- Bring your daily balance back to at least $112,500 to avoid the $75.00 going forward.
- Monitor your balance closely around expected large payments to help stay above $112,500.# ATM fee rebates for Bluest

## Daily ATM withdrawal limit
- Your Bluest Account debit card has a daily ATM withdrawal limit of $1,500. This applies to all ATM withdrawals within a 24-hour period.

## Monthly rebate cap
- You are eligible for ATM fee rebates up to $50 per month.

### How rebates are applied
- Rebates are credited until you reach the monthly maximum of $50.
- If your aggregate ATM fees exceed $50 in a given month, the excess will not be rebated.

### Tips for maximizing rebates
- Keep track of your cumulative ATM fees during the month to stay within the $50 cap.
- Consider using fee-free ATMs once you approach the monthly cap.# Bluest vs. other checking accounts

## How the APY compares
- You earn 2.25% APY on your balance, providing a yield advantage relative to standard transactional accounts that often pay a lower rate.

### When a higher APY matters
- If you maintain a substantial checking balance, earning 2.25% APY can materially increase your interest earnings without moving funds to a separate account.
- A higher APY helps offset the opportunity cost of keeping funds readily available for payments and transfers.# FAQ: Bluest Account

## Frequently asked questions

### How many free check orders do I receive?
- You receive 3 complimentary personal check orders each year.

### What discount do I get on a safe deposit box?
- You receive a 75.0% discount on safe deposit box rental.

### Is there a fee if a deposited check is returned unpaid?
- The returned deposit fee is $0.00.

### Can I place additional check orders beyond the complimentary amount?
- Yes. Once you use your 3 complimentary orders for the year, additional orders are available at standard pricing.

### How do I take advantage of the safe deposit box discount?
- When opening or renewing a rental, the 75.0% discount is applied to the rental charge.# Bluest Account: Out-of-network ATM fees

## When this fee applies
- You are charged an out-of-network ATM fee when you withdraw cash from an ATM that is not part of Rho-Bank’s network.
- The fee is assessed per withdrawal. Multiple withdrawals will each incur a separate fee.
- Any surcharge displayed by the ATM operator is in addition to Rho-Bank’s fee and is not controlled by Rho-Bank.

## Fee amount
| Transaction | Rho-Bank fee |
| --- | --- |
| Cash withdrawal at an out-of-network ATM | $2.00 per withdrawal |

## How the fee is assessed and displayed
- The fee is added to the total cost of your withdrawal and posts as a separate line item on your account activity.
- The description typically references “ATM” or “Out-of-network ATM” along with the fee amount of $2.00.
- If the ATM operator adds a surcharge, it will usually appear as part of the withdrawal amount on the receipt and may appear as a separate charge or be included in the withdrawal total, depending on the operator’s processing.

## Tips to minimize out-of-network ATM costs
- Use in-network ATMs whenever possible to avoid the $2.00 fee.
- If you must use an out-of-network ATM, consolidate cash needs into a single withdrawal to avoid paying the fee multiple times.
- Review the ATM screen for any additional operator surcharges before confirming your withdrawal; cancel and try a different ATM if the surcharge is high.

## Examples
- Single withdrawal: Withdrawing cash once from an out-of-network ATM will incur a fee of $2.00, plus any ATM operator surcharge.
- Multiple withdrawals: Making two separate withdrawals at out-of-network ATMs will result in two fees of $2.00 (one per withdrawal), in addition to any operator surcharges.

# Using ATMs worldwide

## Daily ATM withdrawal limit
- Your Purple Account debit card has a daily ATM withdrawal limit of $1,000. This limit applies to all ATM withdrawals worldwide within a 24-hour period.

## How ATM rebates work
- You are eligible for refunds of ATM operator fees up to a monthly cap of $30.
- Rebates apply after eligible ATM fees post to your account and are credited up to the monthly cap.

## Best practices when withdrawing cash abroad
- Choose the checking account option on the ATM when prompted.
- Retain the ATM receipt if it shows a surcharge to help with any rebate review.
- Avoid optional dynamic currency conversion at the ATM if you prefer to be billed in the local currency.

## Troubleshooting
- If you believe a rebate is missing, verify whether your monthly total rebates have reached $30 and confirm that the charge was coded as an ATM operator fee.# Multi-currency wallet features

## Availability
- Multi-currency wallet support for this account is Yes.

## Holdings and supported currencies
- You can hold balances in up to 30 foreign currencies.

## Conversions
- Currency exchanges execute at the interbank rate plus a markup of 0.5%.

## Sending money with EveryonePay
- You can send funds using EveryonePay up to $5,000 per day. If your payment requires a conversion from a non‑USD balance, the exchange uses the markup noted above.# Travel insurance benefits

## What’s included

- Maximum benefit: up to $30,000 in eligible travel insurance benefits for covered events
- Typical covered events include:
  - Emergency medical expenses incurred while traveling abroad
  - Emergency medical evacuation and repatriation
  - Trip cancellation or interruption due to covered reasons
  - Trip delay and missed connections (reasonable additional expenses)
  - Baggage delay, loss, or theft (with required documentation)
  - Travel accident-related benefits

Note: Coverage is subject to the policy terms and conditions outlined in your insurance certificate. Sub-limits and exclusions may apply within the overall maximum of $30,000.

## Eligibility and confirmation of coverage

- Coverage applies to the Purple Account holder when traveling; additional travelers are not covered unless expressly named in the policy.
- To confirm your eligibility and obtain your policy certificate (proof of coverage), contact Support and request:
  - A certificate/letter of coverage indicating the limit of $30,000
  - Any destination-specific wording required by a consulate or immigration authority

Review your certificate for any activation requirements (for example, required use of your account or card for trip payments, if applicable).

## How to file a claim

1. Stabilize and document
   - Seek medical care in an emergency; keep all itemized bills and medical reports.
   - For theft or loss, file a report with local police or the carrier (e.g., airline Property Irregularity Report).
   - Save all original receipts and confirmations (tickets, itineraries, proof of payment).

2. Notify the insurer promptly
   - Use the contact details in your policy certificate to open a claim as soon as reasonably possible.
   - Ask about any required pre-authorization for medical evacuation or high-cost treatment.

3. Submit required documentation
   - Complete the insurer’s claim form and attach supporting documents (see below).
   - Provide bank details for reimbursement and a copy of your identification and travel itinerary.

4. Track and respond
   - Monitor status via the insurer’s portal or email.
   - Respond quickly to any requests for additional information to avoid delays.

## Required documentation by claim type

- Emergency medical expenses
  - Medical reports and discharge summaries
  - Itemized bills and proof of payment
  - Prescriptions and diagnostic test results
  - If you have other health insurance, an Explanation of Benefits (EOB)

- Emergency medical evacuation/repatriation
  - Treating physician’s certification that evacuation was medically necessary
  - Transport provider invoices and itineraries
  - Pre-authorization approval (if applicable)

- Trip cancellation or interruption
  - Proof of covered reason (e.g., medical note, official notice)
  - Non-refundable booking invoices, fare rules, and itineraries
  - Proof of payments and refunds/credits received

- Trip delay or missed connection
  - Carrier delay/cancellation confirmation
  - Receipts for meals, lodging, and incidentals incurred due to the delay

- Baggage loss, theft, or delay
  - Airline or carrier reports (e.g., PIR), police report for theft
  - Property lists with purchase receipts (when available)
  - Repair or replacement estimates/invoices

- Travel accident-related claims
  - Official reports (police, incident)
  - Medical or coroner documentation, if applicable

## Reimbursement and currency

- Approved claims are typically reimbursed in USD, up to the applicable limits and an overall maximum of $30,000.
- Keep all receipts in the original purchase currency; the insurer will apply its claim valuation and exchange methodology as stated in your certificate.

## Common limitations and exclusions

- Pre-existing medical conditions, unless explicitly covered
- High-risk activities or professional sports
- Losses related to intoxication, illegal acts, or intentional self-harm
- War, civil unrest, or travel against government advisories
- Traveling against medical advice or for the purpose of obtaining treatment
- Non-refundable costs only; refundable amounts and credits are not reimbursable

Always consult your policy certificate for the full list of exclusions, documentation standards, and any per-item or category sub-limits within the overall $30,000 maximum.

## Tips to avoid claim issues

- Obtain and keep contemporaneous documentation (medical notes, carrier letters, receipts).
- Report theft/loss promptly to local authorities and carriers.
- Seek pre-authorization for evacuation or major procedures when possible.
- Submit claims as soon as practicable and keep copies of everything you send.
- Verify that your name, travel dates, and destinations on the policy certificate match your itinerary and passport.# Emergency card replacement while traveling

## Timeline
- If your card is lost or stolen while abroad, an emergency replacement can typically reach you within 2 days, subject to local courier availability and your exact location.

## How to request
- Contact us immediately to report the card as lost or stolen.
- Confirm a secure delivery address where you can receive the replacement card.
- Monitor delivery updates provided after your request is processed.

## Accessing funds while you wait
- If you need a bank‑issued instrument, a cashier's check can be provided for a fee of $8. Availability may depend on your location and delivery options.

### Security reminders
- As soon as you report your card, it will be blocked to prevent further use.
- Update any recurring payments once your replacement card arrives.

## Debit Card Decline Codes - Card Damage and Physical Issues

The following decline codes may indicate physical card problems requiring replacement:

### CODE 82 - Negative CAM/CVV Results (Chip or CVV Mismatch)

The card's chip data or CVV code doesn't match what's on file. This could indicate card damage or potential fraud.

1. Ask: 'Has your card been damaged recently? Have you noticed any issues with the chip or magnetic stripe?'

2. **If card is physically damaged**:
   - Explain: 'It sounds like the chip or magnetic stripe on your card may be damaged, which is causing the mismatch.'
   - Offer / help them to order a replacement.

3. **If card appears undamaged**:
   - SECURITY CONCERN: This could indicate a cloned or counterfeit card was used.
   - Say: 'For your security, I'd like to review some recent transactions with you.'
   - Review recent transaction history to check for suspicious activity.
   - If suspicious transactions found: Follow stolen card protocol to assist the customer.
   - Recommend freezing the card until a replacement arrives.

### CODE 87 - Purchase Amount Only, No Cash Back

The transaction was declined because it included a cash back request that isn't permitted.

1. Explain: 'Your transaction included a cash back request, but cash back isn't available for this transaction. This could be due to the merchant type, the transaction amount, or your account settings.'

2. Advise: 'Please try the transaction again without requesting cash back. The purchase portion should go through.'

3. If customer needs cash: 'For cash withdrawals, you can use any Rho-Bank ATM for free, or use a partner ATM. I can help you locate the nearest one if you'd like.'# Airport lounge access

## Your allowance
- You receive up to 6 complimentary lounge visits per year.

## How to use a visit
- Present your eligible card and a valid ID at participating lounges.
- Visits are deducted from your annual allotment at the point of entry.

## Tips
- Check participating locations before you travel to ensure access.
- Keep your card handy; digital proof alone may not be accepted at all lounges.
- Guests may require an additional visit or separate admission depending on lounge policies.# Currency conversion rates and timing

## How your rate is calculated
- Conversions are priced at the interbank rate plus a markup of 0.5%.

## When the rate applies
- For card transactions, the applicable rate is determined by the network at authorization or settlement. The final posting may reflect the rate at settlement if it differs from the authorization time.
- For wallet exchanges, the rate is confirmed at the time you execute the conversion.

## Viewing your rate
- You can review the applied exchange rate and markup in your transaction details once the conversion completes.

## Debit Card Decline Codes - System and Network Issues

The following decline codes indicate temporary system or network problems rather than issues with your account or card:

### CODE 19 - Re-enter Transaction

A temporary processing glitch occurred. Unlike other system errors, this is typically resolved immediately on retry.

1. Explain: 'This was a momentary processing error. Please ask the merchant to try the transaction again right away.'

2. No waiting period needed - immediate retry usually works.

3. If the retry also fails with Code 19: Then treat it as a system issue and advise waiting 10-15 minutes.

### CODE 91 - Issuer Unavailable / CODE 96 - System Malfunction

Rho-Bank's systems couldn't be reached. This is a temporary technical issue.

1. Ask customer to try again in a few minutes.

2. If issue persists: 'We may be experiencing a brief system issue. Please try again in 10-15 minutes.'

3. Offer alternatives: 'In the meantime, you could use a different payment method, or if you have a Rho-Bank credit card, that uses a different system and should work.'

### CODE 92 - Financial Institution Not Found

The transaction couldn't route to Rho-Bank's network. This is a routing/network issue.

1. Explain: 'There was a network routing issue connecting to Rho-Bank. This is usually temporary.'

2. Advise customer to try the transaction again.

3. If it persists: The merchant's payment processor may have an outdated routing table. Customer can try a different merchant, or use an ATM which uses different routing.

# Blue Account at a glance

## Key details
- Monthly maintenance fee: $20.00
- Waiver requirement: maintain a minimum daily balance of $625
- Out-of-network ATM withdrawal: 1% of withdrawal amount (max $3.00)
- Interest earned on balances: 0.01%
- Mobile check deposit daily limit: $2,500
- Early direct deposit: 1 day(s) before payday
- No overdraft fees

### Quick tips
- Set up alerts to keep your daily balance at or above $625 if you want the monthly fee waived.
- Use in-network ATMs to avoid the 1% out-of-network fee.
- Plan larger check deposits ahead of time if they exceed the $2,500 daily mobile deposit limit.
- With early direct deposit, your paycheck can arrive 1 day(s) early.# Blue Account specifications and requirements

## Balance and earnings
- Annual Percentage Yield on balances: 0.01%

## Fee waiver requirement
- Maintain a minimum daily balance of $625 to waive the monthly maintenance fee.

## Card usage limits
- Debit card daily purchase limit: $3,000

### Practical guidance
- If you regularly approach the $625 threshold, consider setting alerts so you can avoid the monthly charge.
- For large purchases, confirm that the total stays within the $3,000 limit or plan alternative payment methods.# Understanding Blue Account overdraft fees

## Your overdraft fee
- Overdraft fee per item: $0.00

## Daily maximum
- A maximum of 3 overdraft fees can be charged in a single day.

## What this means for you
- Because the overdraft fee is $0.00, you will not see an overdraft fee amount deducted when your balance goes negative.
- You may still notice changes in available balance due to transaction authorizations and settlements, but an overdraft fee amount of $0.00 applies.# Blue Account: Managing your balance with low-balance alerts

## Set your alert threshold
- Enable low-balance alerts and set the threshold to $62 so you are notified when your available balance reaches or falls below that level.

## Tips for effective alerts
- Choose $62 as a practical early warning level that gives you time to transfer funds or adjust spending.
- Use alerts alongside your budgeting approach so you can act before transactions post.

## After an alert triggers
- Review pending and posted items to identify what reduced your balance.
- Add funds or adjust transactions to return your balance above $62.# Why am I being charged an overdraft fee on my Blue Account?

## What to do next

- If the fee appears misclassified as an overdraft fee, contact us so we can investigate and correct it.# FAQ: Blue Account

Your Blue Account earns 0.01% APY on balances.

Yes. When you refer someone to open a Blue Account, you earn $35 for each successful referral. The person you refer receives $30 as a welcome bonus.

The referred person must deposit at least $500 within 60 days of opening their account. A minimum banking relationship of 30 days is required to participate—this is measured from when you first opened any checking account with us.

### Is there a limit to how many referral bonuses I can earn?
Yes. You can earn up to 5 referral bonuses per calendar year.# Transferring funds to another bank

- Verify recipient account details before confirming the transfer.
- Plan time-sensitive payments with the 2 business day window in mind.
- If sending via EveryonePay, confirm that your amount stays within the $2,000 daily limit.# International ATM withdrawals for Blue Account

## Fee for international ATM withdrawals

- For ATM withdrawals made in a foreign currency, you are charged 3% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum fee of $5.00 per withdrawal.

Fee = the greater of:
- 3% of the withdrawal amount, or
- $5.00

## Daily ATM withdrawal limit

## Examples

The following examples assume the ATM dispenses local currency and the final transaction amount is converted to the U.S. dollar equivalent for fee calculation.

| Withdrawal (USD equivalent) | Percentage fee at 3% | Minimum applies? | Fee charged |
|---|---:|:--:|---:|

| $1,000 | $30.00 | No | $30.00 |

## Using international ATMs effectively

- At the ATM, choose to be charged in the local currency rather than converting at the terminal. This generally helps you avoid extra conversion costs set by the ATM provider.
- Verify the total amount before confirming the withdrawal and save the receipt.
- If an ATM displays a message about an additional operator fee, you can cancel and try another nearby bank-operated machine to potentially avoid or reduce those charges.
- If a transaction is declined after cash is not dispensed, do not retry repeatedly at the same machine; locate a different ATM.

# Why does my account have a lower balance than I expected or have a negative balance?

## What can cause a lower or negative balance
- Overdraft protections may temporarily cover transactions, which can display a negative balance until incoming funds post or adjustments complete.
- Authorization holds reduce your available balance while a merchant finalizes a purchase or security deposit.
- Pending card transactions and checks can decrease available funds before they appear as posted.
- Scheduled payments or transfers may be earmarked, lowering your available balance in advance.

## How to review and resolve
- Check both pending and posted activity to understand current holds and recent payments.
- Add funds or transfer money from another account to restore a positive available balance.
- If a hold seems higher than expected, contact the merchant to request a release or adjustment.
- Review and adjust overdraft settings to align with your preferences for coverage and fees.
- If something looks incorrect, contact support with transaction details and timestamps.

## Decline Codes Related to Balance Issues

If your debit card was declined due to balance-related reasons, you may have encountered one of these codes:

### CODE 51 - Insufficient Funds

The account doesn't have enough funds for the transaction. This is the most common decline but requires careful diagnosis.

1. **Check Current Balance**: Look up the customer's accounts to get the checking account balance.

2. **If balance APPEARS sufficient** for the transaction amount:
   
   a. **Check Authorization Holds**: Ask the customer if they have any recent authorization holds that might be reducing their available balance.
      - Authorization holds reduce available balance but don't show as posted transactions.
      - Common sources: gas stations (often $75-$150 pre-auth), hotels, car rentals, restaurants (tip buffer).
      - If holds exist, explain: 'Your posted balance is $[balance], but you may have pending authorization holds reducing your available balance. These holds typically release in 1-3 business days.'

   b. **Check Pending Transactions**: Review recent transaction history and look for transactions with status 'pending'.
      - Pending debits reduce available balance.
      - Explain: 'You have pending transactions totaling $[amount] that haven't posted yet.'

   c. **Check Overdraft Settings**: The account's overdraft_pos_enabled field from the account lookup shows if overdraft is enabled for POS.
      - Regulation E requires customer opt-in for POS/ATM overdraft coverage.
      - If overdraft_pos_enabled is FALSE: 'Your account isn't opted into overdraft coverage for debit card purchases. Would you like me to explain your options?' Then reference the overdraft features documentation.

3. **If balance is genuinely insufficient**:
   - Inform customer of their balance.
   - Offer options: 'Would you like to transfer funds from another account, or would you prefer to make a smaller transaction?'
   - If they want to transfer, help them do so.

### CODE 52 - No Checking Account

The PIN was accepted but the underlying checking account has issues.

1. Look up the customer's accounts to check the account status.

2. If account status is CLOSED: 'The checking account linked to this debit card has been closed. This card can no longer be used for transactions.'
   - If customer wants to continue banking with Rho-Bank, discuss opening a new checking account.

3. If account exists and is OPEN but still getting this code: This may be a system synchronization issue. Advise waiting 10-15 minutes and retrying.

# Why was my ATM fee not rebated?

## Common reasons
- You reached the monthly rebate cap of $30. Additional ATM operator fees in the same month are not rebated.
- The charge was not coded as an ATM operator fee by the merchant or network.
- The transaction posted outside the eligible rebate window.
- The withdrawal occurred at a location or terminal type not eligible for rebates.

## What to do next
- Review your statement to total rebates already received this month and compare to $30.
- Confirm that the charge is labeled as an ATM operator fee and keep the receipt.
- If you still believe a rebate is due, contact support and include the date, location, and a copy of the receipt showing the surcharge.# FAQ: Purple Account

## Frequently asked questions

- Q: What is the monthly maintenance fee?
  A: The monthly maintenance fee is $15.00.

- Q: How can I get the monthly maintenance fee waived?
  A: Maintain a minimum daily balance of $3,750 to waive the fee.

- Q: What are the foreign transaction fees?
  A: Foreign currency transactions are charged at 0%.

- Q: How much travel insurance coverage is included?
  A: Your account includes up to $30,000 in coverage.

- Q: How long does emergency card replacement take when I'm abroad?
  A: Replacements typically arrive within 2 days, depending on location and delivery conditions.

- Q: Does this account include a multi-currency wallet?
  A: Multi-currency wallet support is Yes.

- Q: Do I get complimentary airport lounge access?
  A: Yes. You receive up to 6 complimentary visits per year.

- Q: What happens if a deposited check is returned unpaid?
  A: A returned deposit fee of $20.00 applies.

- Q: Is there a fee to receive a domestic wire transfer?
  A: The incoming domestic wire fee is $0.00.

- Q: Does the Purple Account have a referral program?
  A: Yes. When you refer someone to open a Purple Account, you earn $45 and the person you refer receives $35.

- Q: What does someone need to do to qualify me for the referral bonus?
  A: The referred person must deposit at least $1,000 within 60 days of account opening.

- Q: How many people can I refer per year?
  A: You can earn up to 6 referral bonuses per calendar year.

- Q: How long do I need to have my account before I can refer others?
  A: Participation requires 45 days of checking account history with Rho-Bank.# Out-of-network ATM fees for Purple Account

## Fee amount
- You are charged $2.50 per cash withdrawal made at an out-of-network ATM.

## When the fee applies
- Applies to withdrawals made at ATMs that are not in Rho‑Bank's ATM network.
- Assessed per withdrawal. Multiple withdrawals in the same day will each incur a separate $2.50 fee.
- This fee is separate from any surcharge the ATM owner/operator may charge at the terminal.

## How it appears on your account
- The fee posts as a separate line item associated with the out-of-network ATM withdrawal.
- The posting date may differ from the date you used the ATM, depending on when the transaction settles.

## Example
- If you make three separate cash withdrawals at out-of-network ATMs in one day, your total Rho‑Bank fees would be 3 × $2.50.

## Additional ATM operator fees
- The ATM owner/operator may display and charge its own surcharge before you complete the transaction. You can cancel at that prompt to avoid the operator's surcharge.
- Operator surcharges are set by the ATM owner and are in addition to Rho‑Bank's $2.50 fee.

## Tips to minimize fees
- Use in-network ATMs whenever possible.
- If you must use an out-of-network ATM, consider making a single larger withdrawal rather than multiple smaller ones to reduce the number of per‑withdrawal fees.
- Review on-screen disclosures before confirming the transaction to see any operator surcharge.

Great questions! Here's what I found:

**ATM fee rebates on the Gold Savings Account:** Yes — the Gold Account includes ATM fee rebates of up to **$30/month**, which should help offset those $3–5 fees you're paying on the road. 👍

**Checking account recommendation — overdraft protection:**

I reviewed every personal checking account we offer for a transfer-based overdraft protection feature (where funds move automatically from a linked account — like your new Gold Savings — to cover a shortfall). Here's what I found:

- Most accounts (Evergreen, Bluest, Purple, Green, Green Fee-Free, Gold Years) **don't offer this linked-account overdraft protection feature at all** — transactions are either declined outright or there's no documented protection-transfer option.
- The **Blue Account** is the one that explicitly supports this: you can opt in to Overdraft Protection Transfers, where funds are automatically pulled from a linked account (your Gold Savings) to cover a shortfall. Each triggered transfer costs **$12.50**, and the account itself charges **no overdraft fee**.

Given that overdraft protection is your top priority, **I recommend the Blue Account**. A couple of other details:
- Monthly maintenance fee: $20.00, waived if you maintain a $625 minimum daily balance (if not, there's a fee — let me know if that's a concern given you don't keep much in checking).
- 0.01% APY on balance, 1 day early direct deposit, no overdraft fee itself — only the optional $12.50 protection-transfer fee if/when it's triggered.

Once the account is open, you'd go into your account settings and enable "Overdraft Protection," selecting your new Gold Savings Account as the funding source.

**So, to confirm the plan:**
1. Open a **Gold Savings Account** (5.5% APY, $10,000 min balance — matches your $10,000 exactly).
2. Open a **Blue Account** (checking) with overdraft protection linked to the new Gold Savings.
3. Close your Light Blue Account (no early closure fee since it's over a year old).

Shall I proceed with opening the Gold Savings Account first? And how would you like to fund the $10,000 deposit — external deposit, or do you have funds elsewhere to transfer in?

1. Silver Rewards Card: Understanding Your Included Travel Insurance Coverage
   ID: doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_005
   Score: 21.5296
   Content: ## Coverage Overview
- Per-trip coverage limit: up to $15,000
- Covered incident types: up to 5 categories (for example, trip cancellation or interruption, delays, lost or delayed baggage, or similar covered events)

## Key Eligibility Conditions
- Charge the covered travel fare in full to your card for coverage to apply
- Coverage applies per trip and is subject to policy terms, exclusions, and documentation requirements

## What Is Typically Covered
- Non-refundable, prepaid travel expenses when a covered event occurs
- Essential items during eligible baggage delay
- Reasonable additional costs due to covered delays

## What Is Typically Not Covered
- Known events or foreseen issues at the time of booking
- Non-covered reasons for cancellation or changes
- Losses without required documentation (e.g., carrier delay notices, receipts)

## How Benefits Are Applied
- Reimbursements are capped per trip at $15,000 and depend on the specific covered incident type among the up to 5 categories
- Benefits may be secondary to other applicable coverage you hold

## Proof You Should Keep
- Original itineraries and tickets
- Receipts for additional expenses
- Official delay/cancellation notices or property irregularity reports (for baggage issues)

2. Business Silver Rewards Card: Understanding Your Included Travel Insurance Coverage
   ID: doc_business_credit_cards_business_silver_rewards_card_006
   Score: 17.5848
   Content: ## What your travel insurance can cover
- Coverage is available for eligible trips purchased with your card, up to $15,000 per trip
- Covered events may include certain trip interruptions, cancellations, delays, or baggage issues when they meet policy criteria
- Benefits apply as secondary or primary depending on the policy terms and other available coverage

## Coverage limits and documentation
- The maximum payable amount per trip is $15,000, subject to policy terms, conditions, and exclusions
- Claims require proof of payment with your card and supporting documentation such as itineraries, receipts, confirmations, and official reports when applicable

## Practical guidance
- Keep all travel confirmations and receipts in a single place
- Retain correspondence from carriers regarding delays or cancellations
- Report incidents as soon as possible and follow the claim instructions provided by the administrator

3. Travel insurance benefits
   ID: doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_006
   Score: 16.1354
   Content: ## What’s included

- Maximum benefit: up to $30,000 in eligible travel insurance benefits for covered events
- Typical covered events include:
  - Emergency medical expenses incurred while traveling abroad
  - Emergency medical evacuation and repatriation
  - Trip cancellation or interruption due to covered reasons
  - Trip delay and missed connections (reasonable additional expenses)
  - Baggage delay, loss, or theft (with required documentation)
  - Travel accident-related benefits

Note: Coverage is subject to the policy terms and conditions outlined in your insurance certificate. Sub-limits and exclusions may apply within the overall maximum of $30,000.

## Eligibility and confirmation of coverage

- Coverage applies to the Purple Account holder when traveling; additional travelers are not covered unless expressly named in the policy.
- To confirm your eligibility and obtain your policy certificate (proof of coverage), contact Support and request:
  - A certificate/letter of coverage indicating the limit of $30,000
  - Any destination-specific wording required by a consulate or immigration authority

Review your certificate for any activation requirements (for example, required use of your account or card for trip payments, if applicable).

## How to file a claim

1. Stabilize and document
   - Seek medical care in an emergency; keep all itemized bills and medical reports.
   - For theft or loss, file a report with local police or the carrier (e.g., airline Property Irregularity Report).
   - Save all original receipts and confirmations (tickets, itineraries, proof of payment).

2. Notify the insurer promptly
   - Use the contact details in your policy certificate to open a claim as soon as reasonably possible.
   - Ask about any required pre-authorization for medical evacuation or high-cost treatment.

3. Submit required documentation
   - Complete the insurer’s claim form and attach supporting documents (see below).
   - Provide bank details for reimbursement and a copy of your identification and travel itinerary.

4. Track and respond
   - Monitor status via the insurer’s portal or email.
   - Respond quickly to any requests for additional information to avoid delays.

## Required documentation by claim type

- Emergency medical expenses
  - Medical reports and discharge summaries
  - Itemized bills and proof of payment
  - Prescriptions and diagnostic test results
  - If you have other health insurance, an Explanation of Benefits (EOB)

- Emergency medical evacuation/repatriation
  - Treating physician’s certification that evacuation was medically necessary
  - Transport provider invoices and itineraries
  - Pre-authorization approval (if applicable)

- Trip cancellation or interruption
  - Proof of covered reason (e.g., medical note, official notice)
  - Non-refundable booking invoices, fare rules, and itineraries
  - Proof of payments and refunds/credits received

- Trip delay or missed connection
  - Carrier delay/cancellation confirmation
  - Receipts for meals, lodging, and incidentals incurred due to the delay

- Baggage loss, theft, or delay
  - Airline or carrier reports (e.g., PIR), police report for theft
  - Property lists with purchase receipts (when available)
  - Repair or replacement estimates/invoices

- Travel accident-related claims
  - Official reports (police, incident)
  - Medical or coroner documentation, if applicable

## Reimbursement and currency

- Approved claims are typically reimbursed in USD, up to the applicable limits and an overall maximum of $30,000.
- Keep all receipts in the original purchase currency; the insurer will apply its claim valuation and exchange methodology as stated in your certificate.

## Common limitations and exclusions

- Pre-existing medical conditions, unless explicitly covered
- High-risk activities or professional sports
- Losses related to intoxication, illegal acts, or intentional self-harm
- War, civil unrest, or travel against government advisories
- Traveling against medical advice or for the purpose of obtaining treatment
- Non-refundable costs only; refundable amounts and credits are not reimbursable

Always consult your policy certificate for the full list of exclusions, documentation standards, and any per-item or category sub-limits within the overall $30,000 maximum.

## Tips to avoid claim issues

- Obtain and keep contemporaneous documentation (medical notes, carrier letters, receipts).
- Report theft/loss promptly to local authorities and carriers.
- Seek pre-authorization for evacuation or major procedures when possible.
- Submit claims as soon as practicable and keep copies of everything you send.
- Verify that your name, travel dates, and destinations on the policy certificate match your itinerary and passport.

8. Internal: Lost/Stolen Card - Cross-Product Security Protocol
   ID: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030
   Score: 11.7898
   Content: When a customer reports a lost or stolen debit card, there is a risk that other cards in their wallet were also compromised. Agents must follow this cross-product security protocol to protect the customer's full relationship with Rho-Bank.

## Required Security Check

When a customer reports a lost or stolen debit card:
1) Complete the standard debit card freeze/close procedure
2) Check if the customer has any Rho-Bank credit cards on file
3) If yes, proactively offer to order a replacement credit card as a security precaution
4) Explain that wallet theft often involves multiple cards and this protects against potential fraud

## How to Check for Credit Cards

Use get_credit_card_accounts_by_user to retrieve any credit card accounts for the customer. This will return all active and closed credit card accounts.

## Offering Credit Card Protection

If the customer has one or more credit cards:
- Inform them that you noticed they also have a credit card with Rho-Bank
- Ask if their credit card was also in the lost/stolen wallet
- Offer to order a replacement credit card with a new card number to prevent any unauthorized charges
- If they decline, note in the account that the offer was made

## Why This Matters

Customers who lose their wallet often focus on their debit card and forget about credit cards until fraudulent charges appear. Proactively offering this protection demonstrates excellent customer service and reduces fraud losses for the bank.

## Agent Script Example

"I see that you also have a [Card Type] credit card with us. Was that card also in your lost wallet? If so, I can order a replacement card with a new card number to protect you from any potential fraud. Would you like me to do that for you?"

9. Silver Rewards Card: How to Earn 4% Cash Back on Travel and Software Purchases
   ID: doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_002
   Score: 11.6768
   Content: ## Earning at the Enhanced Rate
- Pay with your card for eligible travel and software transactions to earn 4.0% back

## Steps to Ensure You Earn Properly
1. Use your card directly with the merchant; third-party wallets and processors may alter merchant classification
2. Check that the merchant is categorized in a travel or software/SaaS merchant category; rewards are based on the merchant’s submitted category
3. Allow transactions to post; rewards are calculated after posting, not at authorization
4. Keep receipts and invoices; if a purchase is misclassified, you may be asked to provide documentation during a rewards review

## Transactions That Typically Do Not Qualify
- Gift cards, person-to-person payments, fees, interest, and insurance premiums charged by the bank
- Returned or refunded purchases (rewards are reversed when credits post)

## Visibility of Rewards
- You will see pending earnings soon after posting; final amounts may adjust if the merchant updates the transaction or issues a credit

10. Silver Rewards Card: Which Travel Purchases Qualify for 4% Cash Back?
   ID: doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_003
   Score: 10.4788
   Content: ## Travel Purchases That Typically Qualify
You earn 4.0% back when the transaction is categorized as travel. Examples include:
- Airlines and airfare booked directly with carriers
- Hotels, resorts, and motels
- Car rentals and car-sharing agencies
- Passenger rail (intercity trains), ferries, and long-distance bus operators
- Online travel agencies and tour operators when they are the merchant of record
- Rideshare and taxis when processed under a travel category

## Situations That May Not Qualify
- In-flight or onboard purchases coded as retail or food rather than travel
- Vacation rentals or home-sharing platforms coded under real estate or “miscellaneous” categories
- Parking garages, tolls, or local transit if the merchant is not classified as travel
- Purchases made through third-party payment processors that mask the travel category

## Tips to Ensure Eligibility
- Book directly with travel providers or well-known travel agencies that act as merchant of record
- Review your statement after posting; if an eligible trip did not earn at the travel rate, contact support with receipts for a category review

# Platinum Rewards Card: Getting Started with Your Platinum Account

## Activate and Set Up
- Activate your card as soon as it arrives, then add it to your digital wallet for immediate use.
- Set up account alerts for transactions, payments, and unusual activity.

## Understand Your Rates and Limits
- Your purchase APR is 16.99% (variable). Review it in your account details before your first transaction.
- Typical approved credit limits range from $25,000 to $150,000. Your exact limit appears in your approval details.

## Payments and Autopay
- Choose an autopay option (minimum due, statement balance, or custom amount) to avoid interest and fees.
- The minimum monthly payment is 2.5% of your outstanding balance.
- A late payment triggers a fee of $32.50. Set due-date reminders to stay on track.

## Fees to Know on Day One
- Annual fee: $200.00.
- Foreign transaction fee: 0% on international purchases.

## Virtual Cards
- Free virtual cards are included: Yes. Use them to protect your primary card number for online purchases.
- Virtual card management is available in your account: Yes. Create, pause, or delete virtual card numbers as needed.

## First Purchases Checklist
- Confirm your billing address and contact details are current.
- Enroll in alerts and autopay.
- Add your card to frequently used merchants and services.
- Use virtual cards for new online merchants to reduce exposure.

## If You Are Still Applying
- Minimum credit score required: $750.# Platinum Rewards Card: Earning 10% Cash Back

## How You Earn
- You earn 10.0% cash back on all eligible purchases.
- Returns or credits reduce previously earned rewards on a per-transaction basis.

## Eligible and Ineligible Transactions
- Eligible: point-of-sale and online purchases posted to your account.
- Not eligible: cash advances, balance transfers, fees, interest, and other cash-equivalent transactions.

## Posting Timeline
- Rewards accrue when transactions post to your account and typically become available after the purchase posts and clears any return window.

## Redeeming Your Rewards
- You can redeem once your available rewards balance reaches at least $15.
- Common redemption options include statement credits or other available channels in your account dashboard.

## Tips to Maximize Earnings
- Use the card for everyday spend to capture 10.0% on all categories.
- Set the card as your default payment at frequently used merchants.
- Consider your net rewards after the $200.00 annual fee when planning large purchases.# Platinum Rewards Card: Enhanced Fraud Protection Features Explained

## What Is Included
- Enhanced fraud protection status: Yes.
- Real-time monitoring flags unusual transactions and prompts verification when needed.
- Quick fraud-alert handling with a target response within 17 minutes.

## Purchase Protection Window
- Items you buy are protected for 135 days from the purchase date, subject to coverage terms and exclusions. Keep receipts and order confirmations for claims.

## How Alerts and Verification Work
- When a transaction appears risky, you may receive an alert asking you to confirm or deny the charge.
- If you deny it, the transaction is declined and your card can be immediately secured while we investigate.

## Card Controls
- Temporarily lock your card if it is misplaced and unlock when found.
- Replace your card number quickly if compromise is suspected.

## Best Practices
- Enable transaction and international use alerts.
- Keep your contact details current so you receive time-sensitive prompts within the 17-minute response window.# Platinum Rewards Card: What to Do If You Suspect Fraudulent Activity

## Take Immediate Action
1. Lock your card in the app to block new charges.
2. Review recent transactions and note anything unfamiliar.
3. Report the suspected fraud through the app or support channels. Enhanced protection is active: Yes.

## What Happens Next
- We aim to review fraud alerts promptly, with responses targeted within 17 minutes.
- If unauthorized activity is confirmed, we will replace your card number and assist with disputes for impacted transactions.

## Prepare Helpful Details
- Identify the date, amount, and merchant of any suspicious charges.
- Indicate whether your card was in your possession at the time.
- Provide any travel plans or unusual purchase patterns that may be relevant.

## Aftercare
- Monitor your account closely for additional alerts.
- Update any merchants or subscriptions with your new card details if your number is changed.
- Re-enable your card only when you are confident it is secure.# Platinum Rewards Card: Free Virtual Cards - How to Create and Manage

## Availability
- Free virtual cards are included with your account: Yes.
- You can keep up to 30 active virtual cards at the same time.

## Create a Virtual Card
1. Open the virtual cards section in your account.
2. Select Create new virtual card.
3. Set optional controls such as nickname, spending limit, and merchant lock.
4. Save and copy the virtual card number, expiry, and security code for use at checkout.

## Manage Existing Virtual Cards
- Pause or unpause to temporarily stop transactions without deleting the card.
- Edit nickname and limits to match the merchant or subscription.
- Delete and replace cards when a merchant is no longer needed or if you suspect compromise.

## Best Practices
- Use a distinct virtual card per merchant or subscription for easier tracking and quick cancellation.
- Set conservative limits for new or unfamiliar merchants.
- Rotate or delete virtual cards used for one-time purchases.

- Membership is by invitation only (Yes).
- You should maintain a credit score of at least $780 to be considered.

## How invitations are typically extended
- Invitations are sent to clients who demonstrate exceptional creditworthiness and responsible account management.
- A history of timely payments, low credit utilization, and substantial verifiable income increases your likelihood of being invited.
- Relationship depth with Rho-Bank (deposit history, assets under management, and tenure) may be reviewed when invitations are determined.

## Strengthen your candidacy
- Keep your credit utilization well below industry norms to help support a score at or above $780.
- Avoid late or missed payments and minimize recent hard inquiries.
- Maintain steady income documentation and up-to-date contact information so you do not miss an invitation outreach.

## Important notes

## Understand initial terms

- Each billing cycle shows your new rewards earned, prior balance, redemptions, and any adjustments for returns.

## Redemption threshold
- You can redeem once your available rewards balance meets at least 5.

## Practical tips
- Use the card for everyday and large purchases to maximize the 5.0% rate.
- Keep your account in good standing to ensure rewards post without delay.

- Rewards on a purchase = Purchase amount × 5.0%.# Diamond Elite Card: Maximizing Your 5% Rewards on Every Transaction

## Make every eligible dollar count
- Route high-value purchases through your card to capture 5.0%.

# EcoCard: Apply for a Sustainable Rewards Credit Card

## Eligibility and Requirements
- Minimum credit score required to apply: 0 (0 indicates no credit score requirement).
- You must provide standard identity and income information during the application.

## How to Apply
1. Complete the online application with your personal and financial details.
2. Review the pricing and terms, including fees and interest rates listed below.
3. Submit the application and, if approved, activate your card upon receipt to begin using it.

## Credit Limits Upon Approval
- Initial credit lines are determined at approval and typically range from $5,000 to $50,000.
- Credit line increases may be reviewed over time based on account history and usage.

## Rates and Fees You Agree To
- Purchase APR on carried balances: 19.99%.
- Annual fee: $50.00.
- Foreign transaction fee (international purchases): 1.0%.
- Late payment fee (if you miss the due date): $32.50.

## New-Customer Bonus at Sign-Up
- Spend $5,000 in eligible purchases within your first month to earn $2,000 sustainability points.
- Bonus points are awarded once the threshold is met and the qualifying period closes.

## After You Apply
- You will receive a decision or a request for additional documentation.
- If approved, set up your online account and add your card to a digital wallet to start using it immediately after activation.# EcoCard: How to Earn Sustainability Points on Green Purchases

## Earning Rates
- Green purchases: Earn $5.00 sustainability points per dollar spent at qualifying green merchants and categories.
- Other purchases: Earn $1.00 sustainability points per dollar.

## How to Maximize Green Earnings
- Use your card at certified green partners and eco-friendly categories (e.g., public transit, EV charging, renewable energy subscriptions) to receive the higher earn rate.
- When shopping online, check that the merchant is listed as a qualifying green merchant before checkout.

## Examples
- A $100 purchase at a qualifying green merchant earns 100 × $5.00 points.
- A $100 purchase at a non-green merchant earns 100 × $1.00 points.

## Tips to Ensure You Earn Correctly
- Keep transactions separate: If a cart mixes green and non-green items at a non-partner merchant, the entire purchase may earn at the non-green rate.
- Save receipts for any purchases you believe should qualify as green; this helps in resolving any earn-rate disputes.
- If a transaction is returned or refunded, the corresponding points will be reversed at the original earn rate.# EcoCard: Which Merchants and Purchases Qualify as Green?

## What Qualifies as Green
- You earn $5.00 points per dollar on purchases that meet our green criteria, which generally include:
  - Public transportation passes and fares
  - Electric vehicle charging
  - Renewable energy subscriptions and providers
  - Certified sustainable retailers and eco-labeled products
  - Local bike share and micromobility services

## Partner Network
- We maintain a network of approximately 3 certified green merchant partners.
- Purchases at these partners are recognized automatically as green.

## Verifying Merchant Eligibility
- Look for a green badge in our merchant directory before you pay.
- On receipts and statements, eligible transactions may display a green indicator.
- If you believe a purchase should qualify, contact support with your receipt and merchant details for review.

## Common Edge Cases
- Marketplaces and delivery platforms may process payments through non-green parent entities; in those cases, the purchase may not qualify.
- Mixed carts at non-partner merchants may not qualify if the merchant cannot provide item-level green data.
- Gift cards and cash equivalents typically do not qualify as green purchases.# EcoCard: Exceptions and Exclusions

## What is excluded from the higher sustainability points rate on EcoCard

The following specific merchants do NOT earn the higher sustainability points rate ($5.00 points per dollar) and instead earn the standard rate ($1.00 point per dollar):

### General Retailers (even for eco-friendly product purchases)
- Target
- Walmart
- Amazon

### Thrift and Resale Markets
- ThredUp

### Note on EV Charging
EV charging only qualifies for green rewards when using one of our 3 certified partner charging networks: Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo. Charging at any other network does not qualify.

## Clarifications and tips
- EcoCard purchases at the retailers listed above earn the standard rate of $1.00 point per dollar, not the higher $5.00 points per dollar.
- The exclusion applies to all purchase channels with those merchants (in-store, online, app, pickup, and delivery).
- Buying eco-labeled or “sustainable” items from the excluded general retailers still earns the standard rate.
- For Amazon marketplace orders, transactions processed by Amazon are treated as Amazon purchases and are excluded from the higher rate.
- For EV charging, confirm the charging network on your receipt or session summary. Only sessions on Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo qualify for the higher rate; all other networks do not qualify.

## Examples
- A $100 purchase at Target earns 100 × $1.00 points (not the $5.00 rate).
- An eco-friendly household item bought from Amazon earns the standard $1.00 point per dollar.
- An EV charging session on a network other than Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo will not earn the higher $5.00 points per dollar.

- Minimum credit score: $680

1. Complete the online application with your personal information and income details
2. Consent to a credit check and submit any requested documentation
3. Review your preliminary credit limit offer and terms

## After Approval
- Activate your physical card upon arrival and add it to your preferred digital wallets
- Set up account alerts and autopay to avoid missed payments
- Review your benefits summary, including purchase protection and international fee terms noted above# Silver Rewards Card: Software and SaaS Spending - Qualifying Categories

## What Counts as Software/SaaS
Transactions must be categorized by the merchant as software or SaaS to earn 4.0% back. Examples include:
- Subscription-based productivity suites, collaboration tools, and project management platforms
- Cloud services, developer tools, version control, CI/CD platforms, and code hosting
- Cybersecurity subscriptions, endpoint protection, and identity management
- Design, analytics, CRM, ERP, and accounting software subscriptions

## Purchases That May Not Qualify
- Hardware devices, peripherals, or equipment sold by tech retailers
- Telecommunications, internet service providers, or hosting billed under telecom categories
- App store gift cards and prepaid stored-value products

## Tips to Ensure Proper Category
- Purchase directly from the software provider’s billing portal or official sales channel
- Keep invoices showing the subscription description; if the transaction is miscategorized, you may request a category review
- Avoid paying through third-party processors that may categorize the charge as generic services# Silver Rewards Card: How to File a Travel Insurance Claim

## Before You Start
- Confirm your trip was charged to your card; this is required for coverage
- Review your policy documents to verify your incident is one of the up to 5 covered categories

## Step-by-Step Claim Process
1. Notify the carrier or service provider immediately and obtain written confirmation of the incident (e.g., delay notice)
2. Collect documentation: itineraries, receipts, proof of payment, and any relevant reports
3. Submit your claim through the insurer’s designated portal or the channel provided in your policy documents
4. Upload all supporting evidence and complete required forms
5. Respond promptly to any requests for additional information

## Claim Amounts and Limits
- Reimbursement is subject to a per-trip cap of $15,000
- Individual expense categories may have sub-limits and waiting periods as specified in the policy

## Tips for a Faster Decision
- Ensure names and dates match across tickets, receipts, and statements
- Provide carrier confirmations for delays/cancellations and baggage claims for lost/delayed luggage
- Submit your claim as soon as practical after the incident

## After Submission
- You will receive confirmation and a claim reference number
- Approved claims are paid up to $15,000, less any applicable sub-limits or exclusions stated in the policy# Silver Rewards Card: Making Payments and Managing Your Account

## Monthly Payments
- Your minimum payment is 1.5% of your statement balance (subject to a minimum dollar amount as shown on your statement)
- A late payment may incur a fee of $32.50

## Interest on Carried Balances
- The standard APR for balances you carry is 18.99%
- There is no annual fee: $0.00

## Credit Limits
- Approved limits generally fall between $10,000 and $100,000 based on credit profile and underwriting

## International Purchases
- Foreign transaction fee without a premium subscription: 2.75%
- Foreign transaction fee with a premium subscription: 0%

## Rewards Redemption
- You can redeem rewards once you have at least 17 available

## Purchase Protection Reminders
- Eligible items are protected for 90 days after purchase
- Maximum coverage per claim: $3,000

## Best Practices
- Set up autopay to cover at least the minimum due and avoid $32.50
- Pay your statement in full to avoid interest at 18.99%
- Monitor utilization relative to your limit (between $10,000 and $100,000) to maintain flexibility
- When traveling, consider subscription options that affect the foreign transaction fee shown above
